title: Statistically-Secure Bit Commitment and Coin Flipping Protocols Based on Quantum Hardware Assumptions
abstract: Bit commitment is impossible to achieve with unconditional security, even in quantum cryptogra- phy. We show that statistically secure bit commitment, satisfying both hiding and binding, can be constructed from hybrid locked physical unclonable functions (HLPUFs), a hardware primitive that combines classical hardware tokens and quantum communication. Our protocol uses these hardware assumptions in a novel and non-trivial way to achieve the first mistrustful two-party cryptographic protocol based on hybrid hardware modules. We prove statistical hiding and binding under natu- ral assumptions on the HLPUF and using a carefully designed challenge generation algorithm as a subroutine of our bit-commitment protocol. The construction also yields the first hardware-based coin-flipping protocol. Our results suggest a new paradigm for secure two-party cryptography in quantum networks, combining rigorous security guarantees with a concrete route toward practical implementation.

bite.hook: Hybrid physical unclonable functions enable statistically secure quantum bit commitment and coin flipping.
tldr: Constructed statistically secure bit commitment and coin-flipping cryptographic protocols.
Combined classical hybrid physical unclonable hardware tokens with quantum communications.
Proved statistical hiding and binding under natural hardware assumptions without trusting third parties.
bite.whyItMatters: Bit commitment is impossible in quantum cryptography without extra assumptions. By incorporating uncopyable physical tokens, this protocol opens a practical path to secure, untrusted two-party interactions across future quantum networks.
bite.eli5: Imagine locked boxes made with unique, uncopyable physical fingerprints. Two people who do not trust each other can use these physical locks over a quantum internet to flip a fair coin without either person cheating.

glossary.shortDef: A cryptographic protocol where a party commits to a hidden value and reveals it later.
glossary.eli5Def: Putting a secret vote inside a locked box and handing it over, keeping it secret until it is time to reveal.

glossary.shortDef: A physical structure that produces unique, unpredictable outputs when challenged.
glossary.eli5Def: A hardware chip with microscopic physical imperfections that make it impossible for anyone to duplicate.

glossary.shortDef: A cryptographic primitive enabling two distrustful parties to agree on a random bit value.
glossary.eli5Def: A digital protocol that lets two distant people flip a fair coin together online so neither can cheat.
